Gene Munster Says Meta Needed More Muse Data
Deepwater Asset Management
managing partner
Gene Munster
said he expected Meta shares to be "flat to down" following
Mark Zuckerberg’s
keynote, pointing to a lack of concrete information about Muse adoption.
Meta shares slipped 1.36 in after-hours trading, according to Benzinga Pro.
In a video posted on social media, Munster said the company did not provide the "juicy nuggets" he was looking for on how the AI agent is performing.
Munster said the more important takeaway was Zuckerberg’s long-term vision for Muse, which he described as becoming the "soul" of Meta.
He argued that Meta is moving away from recommendation systems driven primarily by users’ past behavior toward AI agents that can proactively guide what people see, buy and do.
"We didn’t get much on Muse adoption. What we got that was important is Zuck’s vision that all that matters to the company long term is Muse. Bad news for $GOOG," he wrote.

Gurman also highlighted Meta’s virtual keyboard, saying the tabletop-based system "blows the Vision Pro keyboard out of the water."
